_about: Block-name registry: the SINGLE source of truth that maps a `block.name` (architect-emitted, UPPERCASE_UNDERSCORE) to its three derived names — sheet name (used in the parent's sheet symbol + hierarchy navigator + net paths), child filename (.kicad_sch on disk), and human-readable title (shown in the title-block footer). Adding a new functional block family = ONE entry here, zero Python changes. Per IEC 61082-1 / ASME Y14.35 the title block must carry a human-readable title that describes the sheet's function, NOT the parent project's name.
_templates_doc:
Template tokens supported by the engine's block-naming helper:
  {index}              -- 1-based block index, no padding
  {index:02d}          -- zero-padded 2-digit index
  {block_name_upper}   -- block.name in UPPERCASE_UNDERSCORE
  {block_name_lower}   -- block.name lowercased (underscores kept)
  {block_name_title}   -- block.name title-cased with underscores -> spaces
  {project_name}       -- the parent IR's `name` field
_block_name_aliases_doc: OPTIONAL manual override, EMPTY by default. normalize_ir maps an unregistered architect block name onto the closest REGISTERED name DYNAMICALLY — by fuzzy token overlap of the block's own name AND its block_type (regulator/sensor/analog/mcu/comm/driver/io/...) against this `blocks` registry. That is universal and per-circuit-agnostic, so no synonym table is needed. Add an entry here ONLY to force a specific mapping the fuzzy resolver gets wrong (key + value UPPERCASE_UNDERSCORE; value MUST be a key in `blocks`). It is consulted BEFORE the dynamic resolver. Gated by normalize.normalize_block_names.

rectangle_style._about: Visual style for single-sheet block-diagram rendering (the boxed-block schematic style from the user's reference image). Every value here is config-driven; the engine reads `_emit_block_rectangle` from this section. Colours are RGBA tuples in 0-255 (alpha 0.0-1.0).
rectangle_style._uniform_border_color_doc: When set, EVERY block box (border + title) uses this single colour, overriding per-block `color` entries and the default_palette. User wants all block boxes one blue (reference convention), not a red/orange/teal rainbow. Remove this key to restore per-block colours.

_default_palette_doc: When a block has no explicit `color` field below, the engine picks colour[index % len(palette)] from this list. Lets a project with N anonymous blocks still get a rainbow without per-block JSON entries.
